name: Non-specific Autoimmune Supratentorial Encephalitis with Characteristic Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Autoimmune Encephalitis Diagnosis

criteria.description: Subacute onset of working memory deficits, altered mental status, or psychiatric symptoms
Presence of characteristic neuronal autoantibodies in serum or cerebrospinal fluid
MRI evidence of supratentorial brain inflammation (e.g., T2/FLAIR hyperintensities)
CSF pleocytosis or elevated protein supporting CNS inflammation
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, metabolic, or toxic etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Subacute clinical presentation plus detection of characteristic antibodies and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by MRI and CSF inflammatory findings but these are not mandatory.

common.symptomName: Anti-dachshund family transcription factor 1 antibody positivity
Anti-potassium channel tetramerization domain containing 16 antibody positivity

laboratory: Detection of neuronal autoantibodies (e.g., anti-NMDAR, anti-LGI1) in serum or CSF
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers in blood
imaging: MRI brain showing T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in supratentorial regions
Occasional contrast enhancement in affected areas
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoimmune predisposition may be present
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing diffuse slowing or epileptiform discharges

distinguishingFeatures: Often more subacute to chronic course

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline over days to weeks
Failure to respond to standard psychiatric or antiepileptic treatments
references: Dalmau J, Graus F. Antibody-Mediated Encephalitis. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):840-851.
Graus F, Titulaer MJ, Balu R, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016;15(4):391-404.
Orphanet: Non-specific autoimmune supratentorial encephalitis with characteristic antibodies. ORPHA:624166.
